sentences.en: In April 2017, a woman hurried to step off a subway train in the Bronx just as the doors were closing.
sentences.zh: 2017年4月，就在列车门即将关上的时候，一名女子在布朗克斯急急忙忙地挤下地铁。

sentences.en: New Yorkers pull off such near escapes every day, but this passenger was not so lucky.
sentences.zh: 纽约人每天都在上演这种千钧一发的逃生，但这名乘客就没那么幸运了。

sentences.en: The subway doors pinned her in place, half in, half out of the car.
sentences.zh: 地铁门把她夹在中间，半个身子在车内，半个身子在车外。

sentences.en: What happened next was deeply unnerving.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事情非常令人不安。

sentences.en: It wasn't that the subway train started moving,
sentences.zh: 倒不是说地铁列车开动了，

sentences.en: with one of its doors partially open, the train was not going to leave the station.
sentences.zh: 车门还开着一部分，列车是不会开出车站的。

sentences.en: No, the shocking thing, visible in a cell phone video recorded at the scene,
sentences.zh: 不，令人震惊的是——从现场拍摄的手机视频中清晰可见——

sentences.en: was the sight of people walking past the trapped woman.
sentences.zh: 竟然是有人从被困女子身边走过。

sentences.en: The woman was walking off the train when the doors closed on her.
sentences.zh: 车门关上时，这名女子正要下车。

sentences.en: And no one walking by seems to notice or care.
sentences.zh: 而且路过的人似乎都没有注意到或是不在乎。

sentences.en: Instead of helping, one witness recorded it.
sentences.zh: 不但没有帮忙，反而有一个目击者把这一幕录了下来。

sentences.en: Once the video went viral, horrified reactions poured in.
sentences.zh: 视频一旦在网上疯传，惊恐的反应便纷至沓来。

sentences.en: Like, how could somebody just pass by that?
sentences.zh: 比如，怎么会有人就这么无视呢？

sentences.en: People are just caught in their own head.
sentences.zh: 人们只是沉浸在自己的世界里。

sentences.en: They want to do their own thing.
Like, you know, I don't have time, you know.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道的，我没时间，你知道的。

sentences.en: What did that say about New Yorkers?
I would be flailing and freaking out.
sentences.zh: 换作我，我肯定会手足无措、惊慌失措。

sentences.en: In time, a subway employee got the doors open, released the woman, and allowed her to go on her way.
sentences.zh: 过了一会儿，一名地铁员工把门打开，放出了这名女子，让她继续赶路。

sentences.en: But for those who saw evidence of her lonely plight, a question lingered.
sentences.zh: 但对于那些目睹了她孤立无援困境的人来说，一个疑问挥之不去。

sentences.en: A person is suffering, clearly in need of help, and those who see her simply walk by.
sentences.zh: 一个人正在受苦，明显需要帮助，而看到她的人却径直走了过去。

sentences.en: Is this what we can expect from human nature?
sentences.zh: 这就是我们能从人性中期待的吗？

sentences.en: Or is there more to the story?
This week on Hidden Brain, the science of altruism.
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》将探讨利他主义的科学。

sentences.en: Why some human beings perform acts of extraordinary selflessness.
sentences.zh: 为什么有些人会表现出非凡的无私行为。

sentences.en: And how the rest of us can learn to be more like them.
sentences.zh: 以及我们其余人如何能学会变得更像他们。

sentences.en: No matter who we are, no matter how physically strong we may be, and no matter how many resources
sentences.zh: 无论我们是谁，无论我们的体力有多强，也无论我们有多少资源，

sentences.en: we have, all of us will need the help of others at some point.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，我们所有人都会需要他人的帮助。

sentences.en: In the hour of crisis, will someone extend a hand?
sentences.zh: 在危机时刻，会有人伸出援手吗？

sentences.en: Abigail Marsh is a psychologist and neuroscientist at Georgetown University.
sentences.zh: 阿比盖尔·马什是乔治敦大学的心理学家和神经科学家。

sentences.en: She has long been interested in why people help one another, and also why they don't.
sentences.zh: 她长期以来一直对人们为什么会互帮互助、以及为什么不互帮互助感兴趣。

sentences.en: Abby Marsh, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 阿比·马什，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Abby, 30 years ago, you were a college student.
sentences.zh: 阿比，30年前，你还是一名大学生。

sentences.en: You were driving on Interstate 5 to Tacoma after meeting a friend in Seattle.
sentences.zh: 在西雅图见完一个朋友后，你正开着车沿着5号州际公路前往塔科马。

sentences.en: I understand this was an extremely busy freeway?
sentences.zh: 据我所知，这是一条非常繁忙的高速公路？

sentences.en: Yes, it's an incredibly busy freeway, very heavily trafficked.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一条极其繁忙的高速公路，车流量非常大。

sentences.en: I was coming into Tacoma on I-5 South from Seattle when the freeway rises up over an overpass.
sentences.zh: 我从西雅图经由I-5南向进入塔科马，当时高速公路正驶上一座立交桥。

sentences.en: And so there are no shoulders whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 所以完全没有任何路肩。

sentences.en: And yet somehow, a dog had made it onto the freeway that night, and it ran across the freeway right in front of my car.
sentences.zh: 然而不知怎么的，那天晚上有一只狗上了高速公路，它正好跑到了我车前的高速路上。

sentences.en: And I did what I now know you should never do, which is I swerved to try to avoid it.
sentences.zh: 我做了我现在知道绝对不该做的事，那就是急打方向盘试图避开它。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, I hit it anyways, and the combination of hitting the dog and swerving sharply sent my car into a series of fishtails across several lanes of freeway.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我还是撞上了它，撞狗和急打方向盘的双重作用导致我的车在高速公路的好几个车道上连续甩尾。

sentences.en: It's a miracle I didn't hit anybody.
sentences.zh: 我没有撞到任何人，真是一个奇迹。

sentences.en: And then it ended up, as I tried to wrestle back control of the car,
sentences.zh: 在我试图重新掌控汽车的过程中，

sentences.en: spinning in these huge donuts around and around until finally it came to a rest in the fast lane of the freeway facing backward into the oncoming traffic just past the crest of the overpass.
sentences.zh: 车子开始大幅度地原地转圈，一圈又一圈，直到最后停在高速公路的快车道上，车头朝着反方向面对着迎面而来的车流，就在立交桥坡顶的刚过头处。

sentences.en: So your car is now sitting on the highway facing in the wrong direction in the fast lane?
sentences.zh: 所以你的车现在停在高速公路上，在快车道上方向开反了？

sentences.en: And the engine had died as a result of all of this spinning around.
sentences.zh: 而且因为这一连串的旋转，发动机已经熄火了。

sentences.en: And there's no shoulder because it's an overpass that didn't have any end.
sentences.zh: 并且没有路肩，因为那是一座没有尽头的立交桥。

sentences.en: So there was nowhere I could drive the car to or that I could jump out of the car and run to.
sentences.zh: 所以我根本没地方把车开过去，也没有办法跳下车逃跑。

sentences.en: I was just stuck in this fast lane of the freeway with cars barely swerving in time to avoid me because they just, you know,
sentences.zh: 我只能被困在高速公路的快车道上，汽车堪堪在最后一刻急打方向来避开我，因为它们，你知道的，

sentences.en: just caught sight of me as they were coming across the crest of the overpass.
sentences.zh: 刚一驶过立交桥的坡顶就突然看到了我。

sentences.en: And so my car would shake every time these big cars and semis would swerve around it at the last minute.
sentences.zh: 所以每次这些大车和半挂车在最后一分钟从车旁急闪而过时，我的车都会震动。

sentences.en: And I knew, I just knew it was a matter of time until one of them was going to hit me.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我心里清楚，其中一辆车撞上我也只是时间问题。

sentences.en: Well, this is absolutely terrifying, Abby.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这绝对太可怕了，阿比。

sentences.en: And you had no way of moving the car.
sentences.zh: 而且你当时毫无办法移动汽车。

sentences.en: You had no way of getting out of the car.
sentences.zh: 你也无路可逃离开汽车。

sentences.en: You must have thought these were your last moments.
sentences.zh: 你当时一定以为这是你生命的最后时刻了。

sentences.en: It was the most terrified I've ever been in my life.
sentences.zh: 那是我一生中感到最恐惧的一次。

sentences.en: And I remember trying over and over to turn the car back on and I couldn't figure out why I couldn't get the engine to re-engage.
sentences.zh: 我记得我一次又一次地试图重新发动汽车，却怎么也想不通为什么引擎就是无法重新启动。

sentences.en: I remember turning on the brights.
sentences.zh: 我记得我打开了远光灯。

sentences.en: I turned on the flashers just to try to alert people to my presence.
sentences.zh: 我还打开了闪光灯，只是为了试图提醒人们注意我的存在。

sentences.en: But I didn't have a phone because it was the 90s.
sentences.zh: 但我没有手机，因为那是90年代。

sentences.en: And so there was absolutely nothing else I could do.
sentences.zh: 所以绝对没有其他任何事可做。

sentences.en: And I thought that eventually I was going to get hit and I would either get very badly hurt or killed.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，我最终肯定会被撞到，要么受重伤，要么丧命。

sentences.en: So while this is happening, cars are coming by you at great velocity and swerving and missing you at the very last second.
sentences.zh: 所以在发生这一切的同时，车辆以极高的速度从你身边呼啸而过，并在最后一秒急打方向避开你。

sentences.en: Something happens now on the other side of your car, on the passenger side.
sentences.zh: 现在，在你的车子另一侧，也就是副驾驶那一侧，发生了一些事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, one of the great shocks of my life.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是我一生中经历的巨大震撼之一。

sentences.en: So it was a summer night and the windows were rolled down.
sentences.zh: 当时是一个夏天的夜晚，车窗是摇下来的。

sentences.en: And I was very surprised in the middle of all this to hear a knock on the passenger side window,
sentences.zh: 在一片混乱中，我非常惊讶地听到副驾驶座的车窗传来了敲击声，

sentences.en: which, because of which way I was facing, was on the very narrow sort of tiny ridge on the edge of the fast lane.
sentences.zh: 由于我面向的方向，那个位置恰好位于快车道边缘极其狭窄、类似微小山脊的地方。

sentences.en: And I turned to see a man standing outside the car wearing, as best as I can recollect, a suit.
sentences.zh: 我转过头去，看到一个男人站在车外，据我记忆所及，他穿着一身西装。

sentences.en: And he had a shaved head and chains around his neck, gold jewelry and sunglasses, even though it was the middle of the night.
sentences.zh: 他剃着光头，脖子上戴着链子、黄金首饰，还戴着太阳镜，尽管当时正值半夜。

sentences.en: Abby had a lot to be worried about in that moment.
sentences.zh: 阿比在那一刻有太多需要担心的事情了。

sentences.en: But the first thought that leaped to her mind was about the stranger's intentions.
sentences.zh: 但她脑海中闪过的第一个念头是关于这个陌生人的意图。

sentences.en: He asked if she needed help.
And I remember the silly thought flashing through my head of like, oh, no, oh, no, you know, this is a stranger.
sentences.zh: 我记得脑海里闪过一个愚蠢的念头：天哪，天哪，你知道的，这是一个陌生人。

sentences.en: I'm not supposed to let strangers into my mom's car.
sentences.zh: 我不该让陌生人进我妈妈的车。

sentences.en: And he said, you look like you could use some help, which was quite an understatement.
sentences.zh: 而他说：“你看上去需要点帮助”，这可真是相当保守的说法。

sentences.en: And of course, I said, yeah, I do.
sentences.zh: 当然，我说：“是的，我确实需要。”

sentences.en: What did he advise you to do?
So then he said, OK, do you mind if I get into the driver's seat?
sentences.zh: 接着他说：“好吧，你介意我坐到驾驶座上来吗？”

sentences.en: So I said, OK, that's fine.
And I scooched myself over the central console into the passenger seat while he waited for a break in the traffic, which took a minute because, of course,
sentences.zh: 我从中央控制台上蹭过去坐到了副驾驶座上，而他则在一旁等待车流出现间隙，这花了一分钟的时间，因为当然了，

sentences.en: all while we're talking to each other, the cars are still continuing to blow by.
sentences.zh: 在我们互相说话的同时，汽车仍然在继续呼啸而过。

sentences.en: So he waited for a break, ran around the car at top speed, opened the driver's door and hopped in the driver's seat.
sentences.zh: 于是他等待空隙，以最快的速度绕过车子，打开驾驶室的车门，跳上了驾驶座。

sentences.en: So now he's put himself in great danger because now we're both going to get killed if we get hit.
sentences.zh: 所以现在他把自己置于极大的危险之中，因为如果我们被撞了，我们俩都会丧命。

sentences.en: But he figured out the car was still in drive, which is why I couldn't get it to turn back on, put it in park, turn it back on,
sentences.zh: 但他发现车子仍然挂在前进档上，这就是为什么我无法重新发动它，他把它挂入P档，重新打火，

sentences.en: waited again for a break and all the cars blowing by us.
sentences.zh: 再次等待车流出现间隙，而所有的车都在我们身边呼啸而过。

sentences.en: And then he gunned it real fast and arced us across the freeway into the off ramp on the other side or the sort of stripey section by the off ramp where his car was parked.
sentences.zh: 接着他猛踩油门，带我们画出一条弧线横穿高速公路，驶入另一侧的匝道，或者说靠近匝道、停着他车的那片划有条纹的区域。

sentences.en: And there we came to a stop.
And we were more or less safe at that point.
sentences.zh: 到那个时候，我们多多少少安全了。

sentences.en: And again, I remember the sound of his voice as he looked at me.
sentences.zh: 再次地，当他看着我时，我记起了他的声音。

sentences.en: I'm sure and sweaty and shaking.
sentences.zh: 满身大汗而且瑟瑟发抖。

sentences.en: And he said, you're going to be OK.
Do you need me to follow you home?
And I said, no, no, I'm going to be OK.
You know, I wasn't thinking quite straight in the moment.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当时我的脑子转得不太清醒。

sentences.en: And he said, OK, you take care of yourself.
sentences.zh: 他说：“好吧，照顾好你自己。”

sentences.en: And out of the car he got and went back to his own car and drove off into the night.
sentences.zh: 然后他下了车，走回他自己的车，驶入夜色之中。

sentences.en: And that is the last I ever saw of him.
sentences.zh: 那是我最后一次见到他。

sentences.en: Did you even get to thank him, Abby?
sentences.zh: 阿比，你甚至来得及谢谢他吗？

sentences.en: It is one of the things that eats at me to this day that I don't think I said thank you.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，这件事仍然让我耿耿于怀，我觉得自己当时好像没说谢谢。

sentences.en: And I didn't get his name.
sentences.zh: 而且我也没有问他的名字。

sentences.en: So I'll never be able to thank him.
sentences.zh: 所以我永远也无法对他说谢谢了。

sentences.en: So I'm wondering, Abby, did you ever figure out how he came to be standing by the passenger side window of your car?
sentences.zh: 所以我在想，阿比，你后来有没有弄清楚他是怎么走到你车副驾驶车窗旁的？

sentences.en: I only figured it out later.
And what I realized is that he must have been among all of those cars that came across the crest of the freeway and saw my stranded car there.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，他一定在所有那些驶过高速公路坡顶并看到我滞留车辆的汽车之中。

sentences.en: He was the one that decided in the fraction of a second he had to make a decision to pull over into the off-ramp area and then run across six lanes of freeway traffic in the middle of the night to get to my car.
sentences.zh: 他是那个在做决定的零点几秒内决定将车停在匝道区域，然后在半夜里横穿六条高速公路车道来接近我汽车的人。

sentences.en: So he pulls off the freeway, gets out of his car, runs across the freeway, middle of the night,
sentences.zh: 所以他把车开下高速，下车，在半夜横穿高速公路，

sentences.en: comes to your side, gets you to move over to the passenger side, risks his life again, getting into traffic to get into the driver's seat, finds a way to turn on the car, again,
sentences.zh: 来到你这一侧，让你挪到副驾驶座，再次冒着生命危险冲进车流坐上驾驶座，想方设法发动汽车，再次

sentences.en: waits for a break in the traffic, risks his own life to pull the car around to safety.
sentences.zh: 等待车流的间隙，冒着生命危险把车开到安全地带。

sentences.en: I mean, he risked his life three times that night for you.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那天晚上他为了你冒了三次生命危险。

sentences.en: I'm wondering how this left you feeling in the days and weeks that followed, Abby.
sentences.zh: 阿比，我想知道这给随后的几天和几周里的你留下了什么感受。

sentences.en: Well, in the immediate aftermath, I was so shaken up that my mom could tell when I woke up the next morning something terrible had happened.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在紧接着的余波中，我被吓得魂不附体，以至于我妈妈第二天早上醒来时一眼就能看出发生了可怕的事。

sentences.en: I was in a little bit of shock, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想我当时有点轻微的休克。

sentences.en: Dog lover that I am, I was horrified that I had killed a dog.
sentences.zh: 作为一个爱狗人士，我为自己撞死了一只狗感到惊恐万分。

sentences.en: That really ate at me for a long time.
sentences.zh: 那件事困扰了我很长时间。

sentences.en: But more than that, I was in real shock over how close I had come to dying, closer than I have ever come before since.
sentences.zh: 但不仅如此，对于自己离死亡有多么近，我感到极度震惊，那是我一生中从未有过的、至今也没有再接近过的死神。

sentences.en: And that dissipated over time, as it does.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，这种情绪消散了，就像通常那样。

sentences.en: What didn't dissipate is this worm in my brain that I sort of felt at the idea that the reason I had died or been terribly injured was because of the decisions of this man.
sentences.zh: 没有消散的是我脑海里挥之不去的一个念头，因为我觉得我之所以丧命或身受重伤，完全是因为这个男人的决定。

sentences.en: And struggling to understand what caused him to make the choice that he did, to endanger his life multiple times so seriously,
sentences.zh: 并且努力去理解是什么促使他做出那样的选择，如此严重地多次将自己的生命置于危险之中，

sentences.en: to help a person he'd never met and whose identity he could not possibly have known when he made the choice to help me.
sentences.zh: 去帮助一个素未谋面的人，而当他选择帮助我时，他根本不可能知道对方的身份。

sentences.en: Could you have imagined doing this for someone else if the tables had been turned, Abby?
sentences.zh: 阿比，如果角色互换，你能想象自己会为别人做这种事吗？

sentences.en: That's a hard question to answer.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很难回答的问题。

sentences.en: I have never been put in exactly that situation, but I've never done anything so dangerous to help a stranger.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有陷入过那种特定的境地，但我从来没有做过如此危险的事情去帮助一个陌生人。

sentences.en: No, I think it's a very, very rare decision to make, and I have never made it.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为这是一个非常非常罕见的决定，而我从未做过。

sentences.en: So you're still in college at this time.
sentences.zh: 所以你当时还在上大学。

sentences.en: I'm wondering whether the experience changed the course of your college career and what you thought you wanted to study.
sentences.zh: 我想知道这段经历是否改变了你大学生涯的轨迹以及你认为自己想研究的方向。

sentences.en: I had already taken a course in psychology and had fallen in love with the idea that there is a science of human cognition and behavior.
sentences.zh: 我当时已经修过一门心理学课程，并深深迷恋上了“存在一门关于人类认知和行为的科学”这个概念。

sentences.en: But what very quickly happened after that is I started thinking about the psychology of why people help other people.
sentences.zh: 但那之后不久发生的事情是，我开始思考人们为什么要帮助他人的心理学。

sentences.en: Why on earth somebody would make the decision to risk their own life to help another person?
sentences.zh: 到底为什么会有人做出冒着生命危险去帮助另一个人的决定？

sentences.en: And very quickly, my research took a turn toward that specific topic.
sentences.zh: 很快，我的研究就转向了那个特定的主题。

sentences.en: We often assume that people are fundamentally self-interested, that everyone is out for themselves.
sentences.zh: 我们经常假设人们本质上是利己的，每个人都在为自己打算。

sentences.en: How then to explain the fact that some people help others at great cost to themselves without any expectation of recognition or reward?
sentences.zh: 那么，如何解释这样一种事实：有些人甚至在没有任何回报或奖赏期待、自己付出巨大代价的情况下，依然选择帮助他人？

sentences.en: When we come back, the psychology of selflessness.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我们将探讨无私之心的心理学。
您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: At Georgetown University, psychologist Abigail Marsh studies why some people are given to great acts of selfless generosity.
sentences.zh: 在乔治城大学，心理学家阿比盖尔·马什一直在研究为什么有些人会做出伟大的无私奉献行为。

sentences.en: Her interest was spurred by a dramatic moment in her own life when a stranger rescued her after her car spun out of control on a busy freeway.
sentences.zh: 她的兴趣源于她生命中的一个戏剧性时刻：当时她的车在繁忙的高速公路上失控打转，一位陌生人救了她。

sentences.en: Abby never learned the stranger's name, but she realized afterwards that he had risked his life multiple times in order to save hers.
sentences.zh: 阿比从未得知这位陌生人的名字，但她事后意识到，为了救她，对方曾多次冒着生命危险。

sentences.en: Abby, after your encounter with this extraordinary altruist, you became a psychologist and you became interested in altruism writ large.
sentences.zh: 阿比，在经历过这位非凡的利他主义者之后，你成为了一名心理学家，并且开始对广义的利他主义产生兴趣。

sentences.en: Now, that includes people who engage in these kinds of heroic rescues, but also a very select group of people whom you sought out to study.
sentences.zh: 当然，这既包括那些从事英雄式救援的人，也包括你特意寻找并进行研究的一小群特殊人群。

sentences.en: The first group of people that I chose to study to try to understand real-world extraordinary altruism was altruistic kidney donors, or as they're sometimes called,
sentences.zh: 我为了解现实世界中非凡的利他主义而选择研究的第一群人，是利他性肾脏捐献者，或者有时被称为

sentences.en: non-directed kidney donors, who give a kidney to an anonymous stranger knowing they may never meet them or know anything about what happened to them at the time of the donation.
sentences.zh: 非定向肾脏捐献者。他们将肾脏捐给匿名的陌生人，并且知道在捐献时可能永远不会见到对方，也不知道对方的任何后续情况。

sentences.en: And I chose altruistic kidney donors to study in part because it had only very recently become even permissible in the United States to donate a kidney to a stranger,
sentences.zh: 我选择研究利他性肾脏捐献者的部分原因在于，直到最近，在美国将肾脏捐给陌生人甚至才刚刚被允许，

sentences.en: and at the time it was very, very rare.
sentences.zh: 而且在当时，这种情况非常非常罕见。

sentences.en: And luckily, there are databases of people who have donated kidneys to strangers, so I was able to reach out to start recruiting participants that way.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，有一些关于向陌生人捐献肾脏的人的数据库，所以我能够通过这种方式联系并开始招募参与者。

sentences.en: When you began identifying and working with these donors, you were struck by the characteristics they seemed to share.
sentences.zh: 当你开始识别并与这些捐献者合作时，他们似乎共同拥有的某些特征让你感到震惊。

sentences.en: One was their willingness to help you with the research.

sentences.zh: 当你在研究一小群罕见的人时——我在其他语境下也做过——有时可能需要很长时间，甚至数年，才能招募到足够的人来完成哪怕一项小型研究。

sentences.en: When you're studying a rare group of people, which I have done in other contexts, it sometimes can take a long time, years, to recruit enough people to fill even a small study.
sentences.zh: 然而当我开始招募利他性肾脏捐献者时，我震惊地发现：我发出的第一封旨在征求利他性肾脏捐献者、希望愿意参与研究的人能联系我们的信件，

sentences.en: And I was shocked when I started recruiting altruistic kidney donors that the very first missive I sent out asking for altruistic kidney donors to please reach out if they would like to participate in research,
sentences.zh: 是我在动身去参加一个会议之前刚刚发送的。

sentences.en: I had sent right before leaving for a conference.
sentences.zh: 我记得到达会议现场后，大概是坐在酒店的咖啡厅里，

sentences.en: And I remember getting to the conference, sitting down in the coffee shop of the hotel, I think,
sentences.zh: 我打开笔记本电脑检查邮件，结果看到了一波铺天盖地的邮件，全都是那些曾向陌生人捐献肾脏的人发来的，

sentences.en: opening my laptop to check my email and seeing an absolute flood of emails from people who had donated kidneys to strangers,
sentences.zh: 他们以你能想象到的最开朗、最乐于助人的方式主动提出参与研究。

sentences.en: offering to participate in research in the most cheerful and just helpful way you could possibly imagine.
sentences.zh: 来自中西部的一位年轻男子告诉你，他很有兴趣参与，但需要几个月时间来存机票钱，以便能够前来参与你的研究。

sentences.en: One young man from the Midwest told you that he was interested in taking part but would need a few months to save up for a plane ticket in order to come and be part of your study.

sentences.zh: 我说，不，不，不，不，当然我们会支付费用。

sentences.en: I said, no, no, no, no, of course, we will pay.
sentences.zh: 你们不需要自己花钱来参加我们的研究。

sentences.en: You don't have to pay to take part in our research.
sentences.zh: 我们会为你们报销一切费用。

sentences.en: We will cover everything for you.

sentences.zh: 但实际上这表明的不仅是他愿意参与其中，事实上，他还愿意为了参与这项研究做出进一步的牺牲。

sentences.en: But really what it indicated was not just his willingness to take part in this, but his willingness, in fact, to make further sacrifices to take part in the study.

sentences.zh: 而且参与研究本身就是一件很利他主义的事情，因为我们的补偿并不多。

sentences.en: And taking part in research is an altruistic thing to do because we don't compensate very much.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我们无法提供太多。
我们不想带有强迫性，不想支付那么多的钱，以至于人们仅仅为了钱去做这件事，即使那并不是他们愿意做的事情。

sentences.en: We don't want to be coercive and pay so much money that people will do it just for the money, even if it's something they don't want to do.
sentences.zh: 因此，心理学研究在设计上就被设定为需要一点点利他精神。

sentences.en: And so by design, psychology research is set up to require a little bit of altruism.
sentences.zh: 而当我开始招募真正具有利他精神的人时，我才发现利他主义在其中占据了多么大的分量。

sentences.en: And I discovered just how much altruism plays a part when I started recruiting people who are altruistic.
sentences.zh: 那么，一旦你把这些志愿者请进实验室并开始研究他们，你就会发现你所谓的极度利他主义者，

sentences.en: So once you got these volunteers into your lab and started to study them, you found that extreme altruists, as you came to call them,
sentences.zh: 对其他人是否感到恐惧表现出了极高的敏感性。

sentences.en: display a very high sensitivity to when other people might be frightened.
sentences.zh: 阿比，跟我讲讲这项研究吧。

sentences.en: Tell me about this research, Abby.
sentences.zh: 这项研究的萌芽是我之前针对处于我所谓的“关怀连续体”另一端的人群所开展的研究。

sentences.en: The germ of this research was research I'd conducted previously in people who were at the opposite end of what I call the caring continuum.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们在关心他人福利的能力上存在相当大的差异。

sentences.en: So people vary quite a bit in their capacity to care about other people's welfare.
sentences.zh: 而在这个连续体的低端，是那些具有精神病态特质的人，也就是那些性格冷酷并频繁做出反社会行为的人。

sentences.en: And at the low end of this continuum are people who are psychopathic, so people who have callous personalities and engage in frequent antisocial behavior.
sentences.zh: 从对精神病态人群进行十多年的研究所了解到的情况来看，他们往往对其他人的痛苦表现得麻木不仁。

sentences.en: And what we've known from over a decade of research with people who are psychopathic is that they tend to be insensitive to other people's distress.
sentences.zh: 他们很难识别这种痛苦；因此，如果他们看到一张害怕的面孔，他们甚至可能不知道这种表情叫什么名字。

sentences.en: They have trouble recognizing it, so if they see the face of somebody who's afraid, they might not even know what the expression is called.
sentences.zh: 我在英国的一位朋友埃西·比廷曾在一次监狱测试中，测试了一名具有精神病态特质的人识别面部情绪表情的能力。

sentences.en: A friend of mine, Essie Beating, in the United Kingdom was testing a psychopathic person in a jail once about their ability to recognize emotional facial expressions.
sentences.zh: 结果这个人未能识别出她展示给他的任何一个恐惧的面部表情。

sentences.en: And this man failed to recognize every single fearful facial expression that she showed him.
sentences.zh: 而且他知道自己表现得很糟糕，对于一个甚至连精神病态者都算不上的人来说，这也是一种相当糟糕的表现。

sentences.en: And he knew he was doing badly, and that is a pretty bad performance, even for somebody who's psychopathic.
sentences.zh: 因为当看到最后一个恐惧的表情时，他说：

sentences.en: Because when he got to the very last fearful expression, he said,
sentences.zh: “你知道，我不知道那个表情叫什么，但我知道这就是人们在被你捅刀子之前脸上的表情。”

sentences.en: You know, I don't know what that expression is called, but I know that's what people look like right before you stab them.
sentences.zh: 这暴露出一种对他人痛苦的真正的情感盲视，

sentences.en: And this reveals a real sort of emotional blindness to other people's distress,
sentences.zh: 这或许能帮助我们理解为什么具有精神病态特质的人在面对他人的痛苦时会如此冷酷无情。

sentences.en: which may help us understand why people who are psychopathic are so callous in response to other people's distress.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至真的不知道该如何很好地解读它。

sentences.en: They don't even really know how to interpret it very well.
sentences.zh: 而这背后的根源部分在于一个名为杏仁核的大脑结构的缺陷。

sentences.en: And the origin of that is partly deficits in a brain structure called the amygdala.
sentences.zh: 杏仁核是一个复杂的大脑结构。

sentences.en: And the amygdala is a complicated brain structure.
sentences.zh: 它负责许多不同的功能。

sentences.en: It does a lot of different things.
sentences.zh: 但它并非对所有这些功能都至关重要。

sentences.en: But it's not essential for doing that many things.
sentences.zh: 它似乎极其重要的一项功能，就是呈现他人的恐惧。

sentences.en: One of the things that seems to be really important for doing is representing fear in other people.
sentences.zh: 也就是生成那种状态的内在表征，进而帮助你在其他人身上识别出这种状态。

sentences.en: So generating an internal representation of that state that helps you then recognize it in others.
sentences.zh: 我们在针对利他主义人群的研究之初假设：如果那些极度缺乏关怀的人似乎对别人的痛苦表现出异常的麻木不敏感，

sentences.en: And what we hypothesized at the beginning of our research with altruistic people is that if very uncaring people seem to be unusually insensitive to other people's distress,
sentences.zh: 并且这背后是由被称为杏仁核的结构缺陷所支撑的——无论是在对他人痛苦做出反应时的激活度降低，还是其体积较小。

sentences.en: and that is underpinned by deficits in a structure called the amygdala, both in its reduced activation in response to other people's distress and its lower volume.
sentences.zh: 因此，具有精神病态特质的人，其杏仁核平均而言异常地小。

sentences.en: So people who are psychopathic have amygdalas that are unusually small on average.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许那些异常关怀他人且高度利他的人，情况会完全相反。

sentences.en: Um, maybe people who are unusually caring and highly altruistic will look exactly the opposite.
sentences.zh: 他们会对别人的痛苦更加敏感，能更好地识别它，

sentences.en: They'll be sensitive to other people's distress, better recognizing it,
sentences.zh: 并且我们会看到，在面对这种痛苦时，他们的杏仁核激活度会增加，也许杏仁核的体积也会更大。

sentences.en: and we would see increased amygdala activation in response to that distress and maybe larger amygdalas as well.
sentences.zh: 所以这些就是我们出发时的假设。

sentences.en: So those were our hypotheses setting out.
sentences.zh: 这就是你们发现的结果吗？

sentences.en: That was exactly what we found.
sentences.zh: 我们在第一项研究中测试的利他主义人群，表现得与具有精神病态特质的人截然相反。

sentences.en: The altruistic people that we tested on our very first study looked the opposite of people who were psychopathic.
sentences.zh: 他们相对更擅长识别他人的恐惧，但在识别其他表情方面并不更擅长。

sentences.en: They were relatively better at recognizing other people's fear, and they were not better at recognizing other expressions.
sentences.zh: 所以我们也测试了他们识别愤怒的能力，结果他们并没有更好地识别愤怒。

sentences.en: So we also tested how well they recognized anger, and they didn't recognize anger better.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们识别愤怒的能力甚至稍微差了一点。

sentences.en: In fact, they recognized it a little worse.
sentences.zh: 但他们对别人的痛苦表现出非常具体的敏感性。

sentences.en: But they were very specifically sensitive to other people's distress.
sentences.zh: 我们还在大脑扫描研究中发现，

sentences.en: And we also found that in our brain scanning studies,
sentences.zh: 在面对他人恐惧的图片时，他们的杏仁核表现出更强的激活，

sentences.en: their amygdala showed more activation in response to images of other people's fear,
sentences.zh: 然而再次强调，在面对他人的愤怒时，它并没有显示出这种反应。

sentences.en: whereas again, it did not show that response to other people's anger.
sentences.zh: 最后，与我们测试的作为对照组的、并非利他性肾脏捐献者的成年人相比，

sentences.en: And finally, their amygdalas were on average about 8% larger than in a comparable group of adults
sentences.zh: 他们的杏仁核平均要大8%左右。

sentences.en: that we also tested who were not altruistic kidney donors.
sentences.zh: 你发现的非凡利他主义者的另一个特征是，

sentences.en: So another characteristic of extraordinary altruists that you identified
sentences.zh: 他们进行心理学家所谓的“社会贴现”的倾向显著降低。

sentences.en: was a dramatically reduced tendency to engage in what psychologists call social discounting.

sentences.zh: 简而言之，社会贴现反映了你如何根据他人与你的社会距离，来衡量他们所获结果的价值。

sentences.en: So social discounting reflects how you value other people's outcomes as a function of their social distance from you.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是，你愿意为让另一个人受益而牺牲多少？

sentences.en: Basically, how much are you willing to sacrifice to benefit another person?
sentences.zh: 在标准的社会贴现任务中，大多数人都非常愿意为了让亲近的人受益而做出牺牲，

sentences.en: And most people in standard social discounting tasks are very willing to sacrifice to benefit people close to them,
sentences.zh: 但随着人们在社会距离上变得越来越疏远，他们愿意牺牲的意愿会急剧地、呈双曲线般下降。

sentences.en: but their willingness to sacrifice drops dramatically, hyperbolically, as people become more socially distant.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果我有一百美元，要把它分享给伴侣、父母或孩子，

sentences.en: So in other words, if I have, you know, $100, sharing it with a partner or a parent or a child,

sentences.zh: 如果要把它分享给一个完全不认识的人，我几乎完全不可能这么做。

sentences.en: Sharing it with someone whom I don't know at all, very unlikely I'm going to do it at all.

sentences.zh: 纵观不同的测试环节和国家，

sentences.en: And across testing sessions and countries,
sentences.zh: 我们发现人们分享资源的欲望非常有限，

sentences.en: we see that people have a very limited desire to share resources,
sentences.zh: 为了那些不认识或几乎不认识的人的利益而做出牺牲的欲望也很低。

sentences.en: to sacrifice, to benefit people that they don't know or barely know.
sentences.zh: 那么你在非凡利他主义者身上发现了什么？

sentences.en: And what did you find with the extraordinary altruists?
sentences.zh: 当我们让利他性肾脏捐献者完成社会贴现任务时，

sentences.en: When we tested the altruistic kidney donors in the social discounting task,
sentences.zh: 我们发现了一条在任何社会贴现任务中都从未见过的曲线，

sentences.en: we found a curve unlike any that's ever been found in any social discounting task,
sentences.zh: 这条曲线在不同的社会距离之间几乎没有任何下降。

sentences.en: which was a curve that dropped almost not at all across social distances.
sentences.zh: 因此，将肾脏捐给陌生人的人，他们愿意牺牲来帮助一个陌生人的程度，

sentences.en: So people who donate kidneys to strangers are willing to sacrifice as much to help a stranger
sentences.zh: 和大多数人愿意牺牲来帮助介于远亲朋友和泛泛之交之间的人的程度差不多，

sentences.en: as most people are willing to sacrifice to help somewhere between a distant friend and an acquaintance,
sentences.zh: 尽管他们根本不认识那个人。

sentences.en: even though they don't know that person at all.
sentences.zh: 那个人的福祉对他们来说显然具有内在的重要性。

sentences.en: That person's welfare clearly intrinsically matters to them.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这就好比他们认为与自己有联系的那个圈子

sentences.en: So in other words, it's almost as if the circle of who they thought as being connected to them

sentences.zh: 他们的关怀圈要广阔得多。

sentences.en: They have a much wider circle of caring.
sentences.zh: 他们将那些从未谋面的人的结局视为具有内在价值，

sentences.en: They view the outcomes of people they've never met before as intrinsically valuable,
sentences.zh: 认为那是值得关心、值得为之牺牲的事物。

sentences.en: as something that it's worth caring about and worth sacrificing for.
sentences.zh: 你曾遇到过一位名叫哈罗德·明茨的肾脏捐献者，他的态度完美体现了这种社会贴现减少的现象。

sentences.en: You met one kidney donor named Harold Mintz, whose attitude exemplifies this phenomenon of reduced social discounting.

sentences.zh: 哈罗德是国内最早的利他性肾脏捐献者之一，也是华盛顿特区的第一位。

sentences.en: So Harold was one of the first altruistic kidney donors in the country, and he was the first in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 他实际上是捐给了我工作的乔治城大学。

sentences.en: He actually donated to Georgetown, where I work.
sentences.zh: 而且哈罗德是自己萌生了向陌生人捐献肾脏的想法。

sentences.en: And Harold came up with the idea to donate a kidney to a stranger on his own.
sentences.zh: 他以前从不认识任何做过这件事的人，但他知道你可以向陌生人捐献骨髓，

sentences.en: He had never known anybody who'd done it before, but he knew you could donate bone marrow to strangers,
sentences.zh: 他也知道你可以向认识的人捐献肾脏。

sentences.en: and he knew you could donate kidneys to people you know.
sentences.zh: 于是他想，嘿，如果我可以向我认识的人捐献肾脏，

sentences.en: And so he thought, hey, if I could donate a kidney to somebody I know,
sentences.zh: 而我又不认识任何需要肾脏的人，那我为什么不直接捐给需要肾脏的人呢？

sentences.en: and I don't know anybody that needs a kidney, why don't I just donate to somebody that needs a kidney?
sentences.zh: 于是他给几个移植组织打电话咨询，

sentences.en: And so he called around to several transplantation organizations,
sentences.zh: 而他们给他寄了一堆关于遗体器官捐献的宣传册。

sentences.en: and they sent him a bunch of pamphlets for deceased donation.
And he said, that's not what I want.
sentences.zh: 我想现在就捐给需要我肾脏的人。

sentences.en: I want to donate to somebody now who needs my kidney.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间他没有听到任何消息。

sentences.en: And he didn't hear anything for a while.
sentences.zh: 后来他们在华盛顿特区开展了一个试点项目，

sentences.en: Well, and then eventually they ran a pilot program in D.C.
sentences.zh: 尝试非定向的利他性肾脏捐献。

sentences.en: to try non-directed altruistic kidney donation.
sentences.zh: 被选中接受哈罗德肾脏的人是一位女性，她自己的社交圈里没有符合捐献条件的捐献者，

sentences.en: The person that was chosen to receive Harold's kidney was a woman who had no eligible donors in her own circle,
sentences.zh: 其他人也接受过配型检测，当时她正因肾病而濒临死亡。

sentences.en: and other people had been tested, and was dying of kidney disease.

sentences.zh: 靠透析维生就像是活生生的死刑，人们是这样形容它的。

sentences.en: Living on dialysis is like a living death, is how people describe it.
sentences.zh: 当哈罗德决定将肾脏捐给她时，他并不知道她是谁。

sentences.en: And Harold didn't know who she was when he decided to donate to her.
sentences.zh: 他走进手术室，切除了一颗肾脏。

sentences.en: He went into surgery, had a kidney removed.
sentences.zh: 它被移植到了他的受赠者体内。

sentences.en: It was planted into his recipient.
sentences.zh: 移植外科医生将其形容为“拉撒路效应”。

sentences.en: Transplant surgeons describe it as a Lazarus effect.
sentences.zh: 很少有这样的疾病，当你完成手术后，肾脏会立即开始工作。

sentences.en: When there are very few diseases like this that you can perform a surgery, the kidney starts working immediately.
sentences.zh: 它马上就会开始产生尿液。

sentences.en: It starts producing urine right away.
sentences.zh: 而这个人就像是起死回生了一样。

sentences.en: And the person is like brought back to life.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像延时摄影中久旱逢甘霖的植物一样，他们恢复健康、生命力和精力的速度就是这么快。

sentences.en: You know, that a plant that has been watered in a time lapse is how quickly they're restored to health and life and vigor.
And it was a tremendous success.
sentences.zh: 我确信这促成了我们今天拥有更广泛规模的此类项目。

sentences.en: I'm sure it contributed to the fact that we now have programs like this on a wider scale.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，哈罗德和他的受赠者依然是非常要好的朋友。

sentences.en: And Harold and his recipients remain very good friends to this day.
sentences.zh: 关于哈罗德以及你交谈过的一些其他捐献者，令人印象深刻的一点是，这些捐献者通常并不觉得自己身上的利他主义需要什么解释。

sentences.en: So one of the things that's striking about Harold and some of the other donors that you spoke with is that these donors often don't feel like their altruism requires an explanation.
sentences.zh: 当你问他们，“你为什么这么无私？”时，

sentences.en: When you ask them, you know, why are you so altruistic?
sentences.zh: 他们的反问却是：“为什么别人不都这么无私？”

sentences.en: Their question is, why isn't everyone so altruistic?

sentences.zh: 关于利他性肾脏捐献者，最重要的事情之一就是：尽管许多自己绝不会考虑捐献肾脏的人，会觉得选择向素不相识、急需救助的陌生人捐献肾脏是一件需要解释的事情，

sentences.en: that's one of the most important things to know about altruistic kidney donors is that although many people who themselves would not consider donating a kidney find the choice to donate a kidney to a stranger in need of explanation,
sentences.zh: 但真正的捐献者的感受却恰恰相反。

sentences.en: actual donors feel exactly the opposite.
sentences.zh: 实际捐赠者的感受恰恰相反。

sentences.en: They think if you have two kidneys and you could survive just fine with one, which is true, that if another person is going to die unless they get your kidney,
sentences.zh: 他们认为如果你有两个肾，而你只用一个也能活得很好，这确实是真的，如果另一个人如果不得到你的肾就会死，

sentences.en: the choice to donate to them is the obvious choice.
sentences.zh: 捐给他们的选择是显而易见的。

sentences.en: It feels to them so intuitive and so clear that they have trouble understanding why anybody wouldn't make that decision.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，这实在是太直观、太清晰了，以至于他们很难理解为什么会有人不做那个决定。

sentences.en: Another distinguishing characteristic of these altruists was their striking sense of humility.
sentences.zh: 这些利他主义者的另一个显著特征是他们惊人的谦逊。

sentences.en: Can you talk about this idea, Abby?
sentences.zh: 你能聊聊这个想法吗，艾比？

sentences.en: Yes, it was something I was really surprised to discover when I started working with altruistic kidney donors.
sentences.zh: 是的，当我开始研究利他性肾脏捐赠者时，这是我真正感到惊讶的发现。

sentences.en: And I thought maybe how humble they were about their choice to donate was sort of, you know, just a quirky little bug.
sentences.zh: 我曾以为他们对自己捐赠选择的谦逊态度，你知道的，可能只是一种古怪的小偏差。

sentences.en: But I now believe it's an intrinsic feature of the decision to help other people.
sentences.zh: 但我现在相信，这是帮助他人这一决定的一个内在特征。

sentences.en: Many donors I've worked with, I would say most donors, including Harold, have told me that they're happy to take part in my research, they're glad I'm doing it,
sentences.zh: 许多我合作过的捐赠者，我想说大多数捐赠者，包括哈罗德，都告诉我他们很高兴参与我的研究，很高兴我在做这件事，

sentences.en: but they're pretty sure I'm not going to find any differences between them and other adults because there's nothing special about them or anybody else who wants to donate a kidney.
sentences.zh: 但他们很确信我不会发现他们和其他成年人之间有什么区别，因为他们或任何其他想捐肾的人并没有什么特别之处。

sentences.en: It's just a function of having the right information, being in the right place at the right time.
sentences.zh: 这只具有在正确的时间身处正确的地点、拥有正确信息的作用。
这是任何人都能做到的事。

sentences.en: And I've had many altruists reassure me that there's nothing special about them.
sentences.zh: 而且许多利他主义者向我保证，他们并没有什么特别之处。

sentences.en: And that, to me, makes perfect sense because if you really do believe that you're the most special person, why would you want to share with somebody less special?
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这完全说得通，因为如果你真的觉得自己是最特别的人，你又怎么会想跟那些没那么特别的人分享呢？

sentences.en: The most special person should have all the kidneys.
sentences.zh: 最特别的人应该拥有所有的肾脏。

sentences.en: But if you're such a humble person that you don't think you're any more special than anybody else, it does make complete sense that you would say,
sentences.zh: 但如果你是一个如此谦逊的人，不觉得自己比任何人更特别，那么当你这么说时就完全说得通了：

sentences.en: well, why should me, who's not in any way special, have all the kidney resources?
sentences.zh: 嗯，凭什么我这个一点也不特别的人，要拥有所有的肾脏资源呢？

sentences.en: It really makes much more sense to allocate them among anybody who happens to need one.
sentences.zh: 把它们分配给任何恰好需要的人，这显然才更加合情合理。

sentences.en: One of these very humble altruists is the actor Danny Trejo.
sentences.zh: 这些非常谦逊的利他主义者之一就是演员丹尼·特乔。

sentences.en: For listeners who might not be familiar with him, tell me what kind of roles he portrays and how he came to your attention.
sentences.zh: 对于可能不太了解他的听众，请告诉我他塑造了什么样的角色，以及他是怎么进入你的视野的？

sentences.en: I'm familiar with Danny Trejo from his role in Spy Kids, where he plays a villain, as he often does in the movies,
sentences.zh: 我对丹尼·特乔的熟悉来自于他在《特工小子》中的角色，他在里面扮演一个反派，正如他在电影中经常做的那样，

sentences.en: because he has this very gravelly-sounding voice and a craggy face and looks very forbidding.
sentences.zh: 因为他有着非常沙哑的嗓音、饱经风霜的面容，看起来非常令人敬畏。

sentences.en: And so he usually plays villains in the movies.
sentences.zh: 所以他通常在电影里扮演反派。

sentences.en: And so how did he come to your attention as an altruist?
sentences.zh: 那么，他怎么会作为一名利他主义者进入你的视野呢？

sentences.en: Well, he was in the news for something very altruistic and heroic that he did.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他因为做了一件非常利他和英勇的事情而上了新闻。

sentences.en: He was running errands, I think, near his home one day when he witnessed a terrifying car crash
sentences.zh: 我想有一天他正在他家附近办杂事时，目睹了一场可怕的车祸，

sentences.en: when a sedan next to his car collided with an SUV.
sentences.zh: 当时他车旁的一辆轿车与一辆SUV相撞了。

sentences.en: And it resulted in this chain reaction that flipped this SUV upside down.
sentences.zh: 这引发了一连串的反应，把这辆SUV撞得底朝天。

sentences.en: And inside was trapped a little boy who I believe had special needs, along with his mother and his grandma.
sentences.zh: 里面困着一个小男孩，我相信他有特殊需求，还有他的母亲和奶奶。

sentences.en: And Trejo, as is often the case in these situations, reacted immediately.
sentences.zh: 特乔，正如这种情况下经常发生的那样，立刻做出了反应。

sentences.en: He could smell gas trickling out of the wreckage of the cars.
sentences.zh: 他能闻到车体残骸中渗出汽油的气味。

sentences.en: But despite that, he crawled into the SUV, which was upside down at that point,
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，他还是爬进了当时已经底朝天的SUV里，

sentences.en: and figured out how to extract the boy from the car and then sat by him and helped keep him calm
sentences.zh: 想方设法把男孩从车里救了出来，然后坐在他身边帮他保持冷静，

sentences.en: while emergency rescuers got the rest of his family out of the car.
sentences.zh: 同时紧急救援人员把他的其他家人从车里救了出来。

sentences.en: So I understand that when people asked him afterwards, you know, why he had done what he did,
sentences.zh: 所以我听说，事后当人们问他，你知道的，他为什么要这么做时，

sentences.en: again, he didn't draw particular attention to himself.
sentences.zh: 同样的，他并没有特别引人注目。

sentences.en: He didn't single himself out as special.
sentences.zh: 他没有把自己挑出来说得很特别。

sentences.en: His quotation was perfectly characteristic of how so many altruists and heroes describe their own actions.
sentences.zh: 他的引言完全体现了那么多利他主义者和英雄描述自己行为的特征。

sentences.en: people have to understand that God put us on this earth to help each other.
sentences.zh: 人们必须明白，上帝把我们放在这个世上是为了互相帮助。
我们来到这里是为了服务。
我们来到这里是为了迎接。
我们来到这里是为了爱。

sentences.en: That's what we're supposed to be doing.
sentences.zh: 这才是我们应该做的事。

sentences.en: I'm just thankful to God because he let me do that today.
sentences.zh: 我很感谢上帝，因为他让我今天做成了这件事。

sentences.en: I think the implicit message was, it's not about me.
sentences.zh: 我想其隐含的信息是，这与我无关。

sentences.en: I was just doing what any of us should do and what any of us could do in a similar situation.
sentences.zh: 我只是在做我们任何人都应该做的事，也是我们在类似情况下任何人都做得到的事。

sentences.en: So, Abby, your research has also found that these altruists not only feel that strangers are as worthy of their help as loved ones,
sentences.zh: 所以，艾比，你的研究还发现，这些利他主义者不仅觉得陌生人同挚爱一样值得他们帮助，

sentences.en: they also engage in mental processes that orient them toward taking action to help strangers.
sentences.zh: 他们还会进行心理过程，引导自己采取行动去帮助陌生人。

sentences.en: Can you talk about this research?
Well, the researchers who study emotion know that there are different ways that you can appraise emotional situations
sentences.zh: 嗯，研究情绪的研究人员知道，你可以通过不同的方式去评估情绪状况，

sentences.en: or interpret those situations that do change the way that you're likely to act in those situations.
sentences.zh: 或者解读那些确实会改变你在这些情况下采取行动的可能性的情境。

sentences.en: When you see a distressing situation, if somebody's in danger, for example, it's very upsetting.
sentences.zh: 当你看到一个令人痛苦的情境时，例如如果有人处于危险之中，这会让人非常不安。

sentences.en: And sometimes people tend to interpret those situations in a way that reduces their own negative feelings but doesn't induce them to act.
sentences.zh: 有时人们倾向于以一种能减少自身负面情绪但不会促使他们行动的方式来解读这些情境。

sentences.en: For example, there's probably nothing I can do, somebody else will help, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，比如我可能无能为力、别人会去帮忙之类的话。

sentences.en: But there are also hopeful ways that you could appraise situations like that.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些充满希望的方式来评估类似的情境。

sentences.en: For example, I bet that there's something I can do to alleviate that person's distress.
sentences.zh: 例如，我敢说我一定能做点什么来减轻那个人的痛苦。

sentences.en: Maybe I could donate money in a way that would help people like this elsewhere in the world.
sentences.zh: 也许我可以捐钱，以帮助世界上其他地方像这样的人。

sentences.en: And we did find in a study that we conducted of altruists and controls that having a more hopeful appraisal pattern
sentences.zh: 我们在对利他主义者和对照组进行的调查中确实发现，拥有更具希望的评估模式

sentences.en: was associated with being more likely to help people in need.
sentences.zh: 与更有可能帮助有需要的人息息相关。

sentences.en: You may have noticed a pattern in the extreme altruists that Abby has studied.
sentences.zh: 你可能已经注意到了艾比研究过的极端的利他主义者身上的一种模式。

sentences.en: Like Danny Trejo, or the man who rescued Abby on the freeway,
sentences.zh: 就像丹尼·特乔，或者在高速公路上救了艾比的那名男子，

sentences.en: they don't arrive at the decision to be altruistic by thinking through all the pros and cons.
sentences.zh: 他们并不是通过权衡所有的利弊来做出利他决定的。

sentences.en: One of the really interesting things about altruistic kidney donors is even though they do have a lot of time
sentences.zh: 关于利他性肾脏捐赠者，一个非常有趣的事情是，尽管他们确实有很多时间

sentences.en: to make their decision, it's not sort of a flash decision they have to make like a heroic rescuer,
sentences.zh: 来做决定，这不像英勇的救援人员那样必须做出某种闪电般的决定，

sentences.en: they do report that the decision itself was made very quickly and spontaneously.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实报告说，决定本身是非常迅速且自发地做出的。

sentences.en: They discover that it's possible to donate a kidney to a stranger
sentences.zh: 他们发现向陌生人捐赠一个肾脏是可能的，

sentences.en: and that there's tens of thousands of Americans in need of a kidney on the waiting liSt.
sentences.zh: 并且有数万名美国人在等待名单上急需肾脏。

sentences.en: And they often think essentially immediately, I'll do it.
sentences.zh: 他们通常基本上会立刻想到：我会这么做的。

sentences.en: I would love to do that.
So you tell the story of a man who leaped into action without really thinking very much about it.
sentences.zh: 所以你讲了一个男人的故事，他没有多加思索就跃入行动。

sentences.en: His name was Lenny Skutnik, and this happened back in 1982.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫伦尼·斯库特尼克，这发生在1982年。

sentences.en: Can you tell me his story, Abby?
sentences.zh: 你能讲讲他的故事吗，艾比？

sentences.en: Lenny Skutnik was a government worker.
sentences.zh: 伦尼·斯库特尼克是一名政府雇员。

sentences.en: Who, in the early 80s, was carpooling home from his job in D.C.
sentences.zh: 他在80年代初拼车从华盛顿特区的工作地回家

sentences.en: And while he was in the car, a plane taking off from Reagan National Airport
sentences.zh: 当他在车里的时候，一架从里根国家机场起飞的飞机

sentences.en: It was a really horrific plane crash.
sentences.zh: 那真是一场可怕的空难。

sentences.en: And, of course, all the traffic backed up on the bridge,
sentences.zh: 当然，桥上的所有交通都堵塞了，

sentences.en: and Skutnik ended up getting out and walking to the bridge
sentences.zh: 而斯库特尼克最后下了车，走到桥上，

sentences.en: and seeing all of these people who miraculously had survived the crash
sentences.zh: 看到所有这些奇迹般地在空难中幸存下来

sentences.en: but now were slowly freezing to death and or drowning in the icy river.
sentences.zh: 但现在却在冰冷的河水中慢慢冻死或溺水的人。

sentences.en: It was the middle of winter, and the de-icing problem had been why the plane had crashed.
sentences.zh: 那是隆冬时节，除冰问题正是飞机坠毁的原因。

sentences.en: And, obviously, it took Cruz a long time to get to the scene of the crash,
sentences.zh: 显然，救援人员花了很长时间才赶到坠机现场，

sentences.en: in part because of all the backups.
sentences.zh: 部分原因正是所有的交通堵塞。

sentences.en: And Skutnik incredibly decided that he was going to help.
sentences.zh: 而斯库特尼克令人难以置信地决定他要去帮忙。

sentences.en: And he walked down to the banks of the Potomac,
sentences.zh: 他走到波托马克河的岸边，

sentences.en: and I think he took off his shoes and his coat
sentences.zh: 我想他脱掉了鞋子和外套，

sentences.en: and ended up rescuing a woman who had been clinging,
sentences.zh: 最终救出了一名一直紧抓着的女性，

sentences.en: I think, to a piece of ice or a piece of wreckage in the river
sentences.zh: 我想，那是河里的一块冰或是一块飞机残骸，

sentences.en: and bringing her to shore at enormous risk to his own life.
sentences.zh: 他冒着生命危险将她带回了岸边。

sentences.en: And when you talk with these people,
when you talk with these extraordinary altruists,
sentences.zh: 当你与这些非凡的利他主义者交谈时，

sentences.en: you often find that they do not use the language of rationality
sentences.zh: 你经常会发现他们不使用理性的语言

sentences.en: So they're not basically saying this is a cost-benefit equation.
sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上不是在说这是一个成本效益方程。

sentences.en: Perhaps after the fact, they say, you know, this is a cost-benefit equation,
sentences.zh: 也许事后他们会说，你知道的，这是一个成本效益方程，

sentences.en: but in the moment, that's not how they're coming to their conclusions, is it?
sentences.zh: 但在当时，他们并不是这样得出结论的，不是吗？
不，他们几乎总是报告说

sentences.en: that they didn't even think about anything before they started to act.
sentences.zh: 他们在开始行动之前甚至没有考虑任何事情。

sentences.en: That oftentimes, they hardly even realized what they were doing
sentences.zh: 很多时候，他们甚至几乎没有意识到自己在做什么

sentences.en: until they were in the middle of rescuing somebody.
sentences.zh: 直到他们正处于营救某人的过程中。

sentences.en: And that afterwards, they often think,
sentences.zh: 而且事后他们经常会想：

sentences.en: oh my gosh, I could have really been badly hurt
sentences.zh: 天哪，我当时真的可能会受重伤

sentences.en: or something else terrible could have happened.
sentences.zh: 或者可能会发生其他可怕的事情。

sentences.en: But in the moment, no, they're not thinking about the risks
sentences.zh: 但在当时，不，他们根本没有考虑对自身的风险

sentences.en: and costs to themselves at all.
They really act immediately on a very, I think, sort of deep impulse.
sentences.zh: 他们确实是根据一种非常深刻的、我认为某种程度上很深层的冲动立即采取行动。

sentences.en: The extraordinary altruists that Abby brought into our lab
sentences.zh: 艾比带到我们实验室的那些非凡的利他主义者

sentences.en: But her research offers clues that selflessness
sentences.zh: 但她的研究提供了线索，表明无私

sentences.en: might be more common than we imagine.
sentences.zh: 可能比我们想象的要更普遍。

sentences.en: why all of us already possess the capacity for extraordinary altruism
sentences.zh: 为什么我们所有人其实都拥有非凡利他主义的能力，

sentences.en: and how we can cultivate it.
sentences.zh: 以及我们该如何培养它。

sentences.zh: 如果你有后续问题、评论，

sentences.zh: 或是关于利他主义和慷慨的故事

sentences.zh: 愿意与《隐藏的大脑》听众分享，

sentences.zh: 请在手机上录制一条语音备忘录

sentences.zh: 并将其发送电子邮件至 ideas at hiddenbrain.org。

sentences.zh: 阿比盖尔·马什是乔治城大学的
心理学家和神经科学家。

How One Emotion Connects Altruists, Psychopaths,
sentences.zh: 一种情绪如何连接利他主义者、精神病态者

sentences.en: From what we've heard so far, Abby,
sentences.zh: 从我们目前所听到的来看，艾比，

sentences.en: extraordinary altruists seem impossibly different from the rest of us.
sentences.zh: 非凡的利他主义者似乎与我们其余人有着不可思议的天壤之别。

sentences.zh: 但事实上，你却说深深关心他人的能力
